newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rebound but uptrend shortlived - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rebound but uptrend shortlived - brokers.

text.p: After a week of slippages, Egyptian share prices on Wednesday rebound on aggressive buying initiated by a handful of investors whom brokers predicted would get out of the market by the weekend.

Stock prices rose across the board in average turnover of 55.97 million pounds ($16.49 million), sending the Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index skipping 2.1 percent or 7.6 points higher to 370.69 points.
On Tuesday, the index fell to 363.09 points, its lowest level since January 29 and its seventh consecutive fall in a week of trading.

"Prices have fallen to attractive levels and a few investors were just siphoning up any stocks they could get their hands on. The market jumped on the bandwagon," said Walid el-Kholi of El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
Out of the 86 shares traded on Wednesday, 43 gained while just 18 lost. Twenty-five ended unchanged.

"We expect these investors to finish their shopping by Thursday and as the downtrend has not yet bottomed out, prices will fall again a little by Sunday. But trading will pick up by the middle of next week," he added.

Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries was the day's most actively traded share, rising the maximum five percent stipulated by the CMA to 99.75 pounds in turnover worth more than 10 million pounds.
Fertiliser rival Egyptian Financial and Industrial, the most active share on Tuesday, also gained 9.8 to 205.81.

Milling shares, mainstay of the bourse's trading, perked up and most prices bumped against the five percent ceiling cap. Central and West Delta Flour Mills was the most active, rising 4.84 to 101.7 and related firm General Silos and Storage gained 4.95 to 103.95.

Investors also scooped up many blue-chip cement and banking stocks. Helwan Portland Cement was busy in 2.4 million pounds of trading but stocks fell 0.5 to 76.75 while Commercial International Bank rose 3.81 to 80.06 in trade worth more than 4.8 million pounds.
Brokers said a "buy" recommendation for the bank's global depositary receipt offering from international securities house INGBarings was behind the increased activity.
The index for openly traded firms also looked up on Wednesday and ended at 575.37 from 555.2 points in the previous day. The index for rarely traded "closed" firms also rose to 255.88 from 252.89.
